newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee higher, London seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee higher, London seen rising.

text.p: Indonesian Robusta coffee prices were higher on Monday, with supply remaining tight despite a slight improvement in bean arrivals, traders said.
They said the local price for grade four robusta was quoted at 3,375-3,450 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, compared with 3,350-3,400 rupiah a week ago.
The traders said the export price was at $1,450-$1,500 rupiah/tonne, unchanged from last week.
They said they expected London coffee futures to open between $20 to $30 higher later on Monday, following a rebound in New York prices last Friday.

"The local prices are staying firm because supply is still tight," one broker said. "Some farmers are selling as soon as they dry the beans because they need the cash or prices are attractive. Others do not seem to be in a hurry as they anticipate prices will go higher," he added.
The trader said there were some buyers offering to buy at $260-$270 below London prices, but added that there were no takers at those levels.
"I will be making a loss at those offer prices because local robusta prices are high," he said. "Furthermore, supply is tight and there are administrative charges I have to bear."
Another trader said bean arrivals in Lampung were improving as the harvest proceeded, but added supply was generally tight.
"I have been getting reports of a decline in production from several farmers in the Lampung region," he said. "The degree of decline is varied, but the smallest fall was by 10 percent."

Traders said they expected London futures to open higher later on Monday following a rebound last Friday in New York, where prices surged 4.10 cents per lb higher to 186.35 cents before long liquidation ahead of the weekend pared gains.
